title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 195 (Agent’s duty in naming such person)

content.overview: In selecting such agent for his principal, an agent is bound to exercise the same amount of discretion as a man of ordinary prudence would exercise in his own case; and, if he does this, he is not responsible to the principal for the acts or negligence of the agent so selected.
content.glance: When naming another agent for the principal, the agent must use ordinary prudence; if he does, he is not responsible for the selected person’s acts or negligence.
content.study: In selecting such agent for his principal, an agent is bound to exercise the same amount of discretion as a man of ordinary prudence would exercise in his own case; and, if he does this, he is not responsible to the principal for the acts or negligence of the agent so selected. Connected: s. 194 (substituted agent relation).

sections.heading: Ordinary prudence in selection
sections.body: Exercise the same discretion as a man of ordinary prudence would in his own case.

sections.heading: No responsibility if duty met
sections.body: If that duty is met, agent is not responsible for acts or negligence of the person selected.

provisions.title: Agent’s duty in naming such person

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 195 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Test whether the selecting agent used ordinary prudence; if yes, no responsibility for the selected person’s acts or negligence.
